{{Short description|Area formula from geometric measure theory}}

In [[geometric measure theory]] the '''area formula''' relates the [[Hausdorff measure]] of the image of a [[Lipschitz map]], while accounting for multiplicity, to the integral of the [[Jacobian matrix and determinant|Jacobian]] of the map. It is one of the fundamental results of the field that has connections, for example, to rectifiability and [[Sard's theorem]].

Definition: Given <math>f\colon \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^m</math> and <math>A\subset \mathbb{R}^n </math>, the multiplicity function <math>N(f,A,y), \, y\in \mathbb{R}^m </math>, is the (possibly infinite) number of points in the preimage <math>f^{-1}(y)\cap A</math>. The multiplicity function is also called the Banach indicatrix. Note that <math>N(f,A,y) = \mathcal{H}^0(f^{-1}(y)\cap A)</math>. Here, <math>\mathcal{H}^n</math> denotes the ''n''-dimensional [[Hausdorff measure]], and <math>\mathcal{L}^n</math> will denote the ''n''-dimensional [[Lebesgue measure]].

Theorem: If <math>f\colon \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^m</math> is Lipschitz and <math>n\leq m</math>, then for any measurable <math>A\subset \mathbb{R}^n</math>,
<math display="block">\int_A {J}(Df(x))\,  d \mathcal{L}^n(x) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^m} N(f,A,y) \, d\mathcal{H}^n(y)  \, ,</math>
where
<math display="block">{J}(Df(x))=\sqrt{\det(Df(x)^tDf(x))}</math>
is the Jacobian of <math>Df(x)</math>.

The measurability of the multiplicity function is part of the claim. The Jacobian is defined almost everywhere by [[Rademacher's differentiability theorem]].

The theorem was proved first by [[Herbert Federer]] {{harv|Federer|1969}}.
